title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff during regional failover to prevent thrashing
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: This hotfix addresses a regression in the SLO enforcer backoff logic that caused rapid thrashing between regional failover and local recovery during a multi-region outage. The bug led to repeated circuit-breaker toggles and aggressive load-shedding that increased user-visible errors during the incident INC-2026-02-21.

Motivation and impact: During a partial region outage, the enforcer would reduce allowed request windows but then immediately reset back to higher capacity when an upstream health probe succeeded briefly. This allowed a tight loop of failover and recovery which exhausted capacity in the healthy region and amplified errors. This PR introduces a conservative backoff window on enforcer state transitions, preserves per-customer rate limits during failover, and adds metrics/alerts to detect thrash. The change is intentionally small and guarded so it can be rolled back quickly if needed.

What I changed: 1) Add exponential backoff with capped jitter to enforcer transition logic (enforcer/transition.go). 2) Make the region-failover coordinator maintain sticky primary preference for N seconds after a successful probe, to avoid immediate flip-flops (coordinator/failover_manager.go). 3) Add a new metric enforcer.transition_backoff_seconds and an alert rule that fires when average backoff exceeds threshold. 4) Tighten unit and integration tests to cover quick probe flaps.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduced the thrash scenario with a test harness
- [x] Added unit + integration tests
- [x] Added metrics and alerting rule
- [x] Ran canary against staging regional failover harness
- [x] Confirmed no customer-visible regressions in canary

Rollout plan: squash-merge to main and prioritize a patch release to release/2026-02. We will monitor enforcer.transition_backoff_seconds and error-rate by region for 24 hours post-merge. If anomalies occur, rollback/revert patch and engage SRE.

Related: previously observed in PR #81234 and tied to Linear ENG-9123. See incident notes in SUP-7789 for reproduction steps.
